name: APT28 (Fancy Bear)
description: Russian military intelligence (GRU) hacking group active since mid-2000s. Known for targeting NATO governments, military organizations, and political entities.

name: APT29 (Cozy Bear)
description: Russian Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) group known for sophisticated long-term intrusions into government and defense networks. Responsible for the SolarWinds supply chain attack.

name: APT41 (Double Dragon)
description: Chinese state-sponsored group conducting both espionage and financially motivated cybercrime. Known for supply chain attacks and gaming industry targeting.

name: Lazarus Group
description: North Korean state-sponsored group linked to the Reconnaissance General Bureau. Responsible for major financial heists including cryptocurrency theft and the Sony Pictures hack.

name: Sandworm
description: GRU Unit 74455 responsible for destructive attacks including NotPetya, attacks on Ukrainian power grid, and Olympic Destroyer. Considered one of the most aggressive threat actors.

name: Turla
description: Russian FSB group known for sophisticated cyber-espionage campaigns targeting governments, embassies, and military networks worldwide since at least 2004.

name: Kimsuky
description: North Korean APT group focused on intelligence gathering, targeting South Korean government, think tanks, and nuclear energy organizations.

name: MuddyWater
description: Iranian MOIS-linked group targeting telecommunications, government, and defense sectors across the Middle East, Europe, and North America.

name: Charming Kitten
description: Iranian IRGC-linked group conducting phishing and credential theft against journalists, academics, human rights activists, and government officials.

name: Volt Typhoon
description: Chinese state-sponsored group focused on critical infrastructure targeting, particularly US military and communications. Known for living-off-the-land techniques.

name: Salt Typhoon
description: Chinese threat actor responsible for major breaches of US telecommunications providers, targeting wiretap systems and communications of senior government officials.

name: Flax Typhoon
description: Chinese state-sponsored group targeting Taiwanese organizations and critical infrastructure sectors using legitimate software for persistence.

name: Scattered Spider
description: English-speaking cybercriminal group known for sophisticated social engineering, SIM swapping, and ransomware attacks against major corporations including MGM Resorts and Caesars Entertainment.

name: FIN7
description: Prolific financially motivated group known for targeting retail, hospitality, and restaurant sectors through sophisticated phishing and point-of-sale malware.

name: FIN11
description: Financially motivated group known for large-scale phishing campaigns and deployment of Clop ransomware, targeting financial and healthcare sectors.

name: TA505
description: Prolific threat actor operating large-scale malware distribution campaigns including Dridex and Clop ransomware.

name: TA577
description: Cybercriminal group known for high-volume phishing campaigns distributing QakBot and other malware.

name: TA569
description: Threat actor operating SocGholish (FakeUpdates) malware distribution network through compromised websites.

name: Wizard Spider
description: Russian-speaking cybercriminal group operating TrickBot and Conti ransomware. Known for targeting hospitals during the COVID-19 pandemic.

name: LockBit Gang
description: Operators of the LockBit ransomware-as-a-service platform, one of the most prolific ransomware groups globally before law enforcement disruption in 2024.

name: BlackCat Operators
description: Operators of the ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware, responsible for major attacks including Change Healthcare and MGM Resorts.

name: Cl0p Gang
description: Cybercriminal group behind the Clop ransomware, known for mass exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities in MOVEit, GoAnywhere, and Accellion products.

name: REvil
description: Russian ransomware-as-a-service operation responsible for attacks on Kaseya, JBS Foods, and Travelex. Disrupted by law enforcement in 2022.

name: DarkSide
description: Ransomware group responsible for the Colonial Pipeline attack in 2021, causing widespread fuel shortages across the US East Coast.

name: Star Blizzard
description: Russian FSB-linked group conducting targeted spear-phishing against NGOs, journalists, and academic researchers.

name: Mustang Panda
description: Chinese APT group targeting Southeast Asian governments, NGOs, and minorities using PlugX malware.

name: OceanLotus
description: Vietnamese state-sponsored group conducting espionage against foreign governments, dissidents, and journalists across Southeast Asia.

name: SideWinder
description: Suspected Indian state-sponsored group targeting military and government organizations in Pakistan, China, Nepal, and Afghanistan.

name: Gamaredon
description: Russian FSB-linked group almost exclusively targeting Ukrainian government, military, and critical infrastructure with high-volume phishing campaigns.

name: BlackTech
description: Chinese APT group targeting tech, media, and telecommunications companies in East Asia, particularly Japan and Taiwan.

name: Rhysida Gang
description: Ransomware group that emerged in 2023, targeting healthcare, education, and government sectors. Known for double-extortion tactics.

name: Akira Gang
description: Ransomware-as-a-service operation active since 2023, targeting SMBs across multiple sectors with double-extortion tactics.

name: Play Gang
description: Ransomware group targeting enterprise networks, known for exploiting Exchange vulnerabilities and using double-extortion.

name: BianLian Gang
description: Ransomware group that shifted from encryption-based to pure extortion model, targeting healthcare, professional services, and critical infrastructure.

name: Medusa Gang
description: Ransomware group known for maintaining a public Telegram channel to pressure victims and publish stolen data.

name: 8Base
description: Ransomware group that surged in activity in 2023, targeting SMBs with Phobos ransomware and operating a data leak site.

name: Hunters International
description: Ransomware group that appeared in late 2023, believed to be a rebranded or spin-off of the Hive ransomware operation.

name: NoName057(16)
description: Pro-Russian hacktivist group conducting DDoS attacks against Ukraine and Western governments supporting Ukraine.

name: Anonymous Sudan
description: Hacktivist group conducting large-scale DDoS attacks, suspected of ties to Russian interests despite its name. Targeted Microsoft, Telegram, and US hospitals.

name: Killnet
description: Pro-Russian hacktivist group conducting DDoS attacks against governments and organizations supporting Ukraine.

name: Fancy Lazarus
description: Group conducting ransom DDoS (RDoS) campaigns threatening organizations with DDoS attacks unless ransom is paid.

name: UNC3886
description: Sophisticated Chinese espionage group targeting VMware ESXi hypervisors and network edge devices with novel malware families.

name: UNC4736
description: North Korean-linked group responsible for the 3CX supply chain attack in 2023.

name: Evil Corp
description: Russian cybercriminal organization led by Maksim Yakubets, responsible for Dridex banking trojan and WastedLocker ransomware. Under US Treasury OFAC sanctions.

name: Ember Bear
description: Russian GRU-linked group conducting destructive attacks against Ukrainian targets, associated with WhisperGate wiper malware.
